notes:
I went through all 64 stations. Six lights change between the 1879 and 1887 editions: Scurdie Ness, Isle of May, Monach Isles, Ushenish, Barra Head and Sanda. Dubh Artach changes only in one sector, and Mull of Galloway is a doubtful change. Three lights are new: Fidra (1885), Ailsa Craig (1886) and North Carr L.V. (1887). Hynish Signal Tower shows no light. None of the stations in this file has a report1880 witness.

Things to check:
1. Scurdie Ness: Findlay 1887 dates the change to occulting 1885, but Edwards (March 1884) already calls the light occulting. I took Findlay's 1885 and let the spans overlap 1884–1885.
2. Isle of May: the change to an electric 4-flash light is undated. The witnesses only say after March 1884 and before the 1887 edition. Other sources commonly give late 1886; confirm it and the window narrows.
3. Barra Head: changed from a 3-minute to a 1-minute period between 1879 and March 1884 (the report of 1879 and Edwards bracket it). Findlay 1887 gives no alteration year.
4. Dubh Artach: the red sector toward Iona became an occulting white sector between 1879 and March 1884; no source gives the year. The main fixed white light is unchanged. Decide whether your drawing shows sectors; if it doesn't, treat this light as unchanged.
5. Mull of Galloway: Findlay 1879 gives a ½ min eclipse; Edwards and Findlay 1887 give ¼ min, and there is no alteration year. This may be a misprint in 1879 rather than a change. Low confidence.
6. Isle Ornsay: Findlay 1879's character says 'br. or red', but nothing else mentions red. I treated it as a slip and the light as unchanged.
7. Chanonry Point: the report of 1879 copies Covesea's line, the slip already known. Findlay is followed.
8. North Carr L.V. and Ailsa Craig: the reports list both from 1885, but Findlay dates North Carr 1887 (and calls it only 'proposed') and Ailsa Craig 1886. The spans start at Findlay's years, so no light is drawn for the earlier report years until you settle this.
9. Lights in Findlay's entries that are not the station's own, so don't draw them: the Lerwick pier light under Bressay, the Stornoway wharf gas light under Arnish Point, and the Lamlash pier red light under Holy Isle. Holy Isle's 1887 alteration year 1880 is also unexplained.
10. Shared entries: Hoy High and Hoy Low use one Findlay entry, item 1 for the high light and item 2 for the low.
11. Misread or misprinted figures that don't affect the character: Buchan Ness '15 ft' (115), Butt of Lewis '20 ft' (120), Isle of May '36' vs '86' ft, Lamlash '[?]877', Little Ross '184[?]', and the two editions' different build years for Portpatrick.
12. Wording conventions: Edwards's 'intermittent' and 'occulting' and Findlay 1887's 'interm.' all mean a light that is bright longer than it is dark. For a light that changed within a year, both spans include that year.
